summary.headline: Infosys narrowed FY27 revenue growth guidance to 1%-2% cc from 1.5%-3%, citing pricing pressure and softer volumes, while Q2 AI revenue hit 10.5% of revenue, up 29% QoQ.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue grew 1.5% YoY and 1.2% QoQ in constant currency, with operating margin stable at 21%. Management cut the full-year revenue growth guidance to 1%-2% cc, blaming pricing pressure from competitive intensity, softer volumes, and weak discretionary spend in Retail and Hi-Tech, plus offshoring shift and a walked-away European manufacturing deal. Large deal TCV was $5.2 bn (62% net new), including a $2 bn+ seven-year net-new mega deal expected to add over 1% to FY28 growth. Operating margin guidance held at 20%-22%, with H2 headwinds from wage hikes, pricing and AI productivity sharing, partly offset by Project Maximus.

financial_highlights.change: Second-highest quarterly TCV in five years
down 7 days YoY; incl. unbilled 77 days, down 10 days

segments.name: Financial Services
segments.commentary: Large deal signings above $3.5 bn in Q2 with seven FS deals; management called FS a strong vertical, though mortgage expected to slow on rate-hike expectations.

segments.name: Manufacturing
segments.commentary: Near-term pressure from lower revenue at a large client, with Middle East conflict, inflation and tariffs extending decision cycles; five large deals won in Q2.

segments.name: Energy, Utilities, Resources & Services (EURS)
segments.commentary: Stable demand concentrated on targeted programs; large deal pipeline has grown significantly over the past year. Management expects FS and EURS to grow above company average.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Sequential decline driven by lower third-party revenue and client ramp-downs from soft consumer demand; consumer tech and logistics most affected.

segments.name: Hi-Tech
segments.commentary: Weakness mainly tied to one US client ramp-down and lower third-party revenue; management says it is largely US-specific.

segments.name: Communications
segments.commentary: Challenging demand with tight discretionary control; AI productivity expectations pressuring pricing and delivery model.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance revised to 1%-2% YoY cc from prior 1.5%-3%; lower end assumes further macro deterioration, upper end assumes improvement.
FY27 operating margin guidance unchanged at 20%-22%.

H2 margin headwinds: wage hikes (most effective October 2026, next phase January 2027), softer revenue seasonality, AI productivity sharing, and ramp-up of large deals; partly offset by Project Maximus.
Effective tax rate for FY27 expected at 29%-30%.
Offshoring impact and the walked-away European manufacturing deal together cost roughly 1.8%-2% of FY27 growth; the bulk of the manufacturing client impact lands in Q4.
Mega deal expected to contribute over 1% revenue growth in FY28; transition begins in the second half of Q4 FY27 with no real margin impact this year.
Capital allocation: 85% of free cash flow returned over five years via dividends and buybacks; interim dividend Rs 26.
capex_capacity: Utilization incl. trainees 85.4%, excluding trainees 81.9% due to fresher intake; management views 85% as optimum with limited headroom.
Net headcount up about 4,400 in H1; about 13,000 freshers hired in H1 against a target of around 20,000 for FY27.
Attrition about 12.7%; management estimates roughly 45,000 annual leavers to be backfilled.
Subcontractor cost held at 8%-9% of revenue (8.9% cited); management says reducing subcontractors by 1% of revenue would add 15-20 bps margin, with a floor around 5%-6%.
Frontier model partnerships and Topaz Fabric (15 foundation models) underpin AI delivery; FDE build-out of 6,000 over multiple years is progressing.
Project Maximus contributed 20 bps to Q2 margin.
demand_pricing: Pricing pressure from competitive intensity: the expected price increase at the start of the year did not materialize; management says peers are more aggressive on pricing.
Volumes softer than expected in Q2; discretionary spend selective, especially in Retail and Hi-Tech.
AI productivity demands from clients are passed through into pricing; management says the intensity has not changed, but AI-related productivity is now more widely exposed across the portfolio.
Management says the productivity effect is finite, while AI growth is secular; the vast majority of AI productivity benefit is already baked into large renewals signed.
Large deal margins are said to be similar to past deals; AI revenue margin not disclosed externally.
North America softer, Europe and rest of world stronger; India revenue up in Q2 on seasonality.

qa_highlights.question: Why narrow the guidance band and what drove the revision from 1.5%-3%?
qa_highlights.answer: Pricing pressure from competitive intensity, softer volumes, and slower discretionary spend in Retail and Hi-Tech; offshoring and the walked-away European manufacturing deal together account for roughly 1.8%-2% of growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is AI-led productivity worsening and how much AI revenue growth is there?
qa_highlights.answer: Productivity expectations are similar to before, with broader exposure across the portfolio; management cited 5.5% AI share at its Q3 FY26 AI Day as a proxy base for YoY, and AI revenue is described as new revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Will the mega deal lift next year's growth and what are the margins?
qa_highlights.answer: The $2 bn+ net-new deal is expected to add over 1% to FY28 growth, with a transition starting in the second half of Q4 FY27 and no real margin impact this year; no asset takeovers, some people transfers.

qa_highlights.question: Is Hi-Tech weakness the start of deflation spreading to other sectors?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Hi-Tech is mostly one US client ramp-down; FS, Energy Utilities, parts of Manufacturing and Healthcare are growing with strong discretionary spend.

qa_highlights.question: Is subcontractor cost a margin drag?
qa_highlights.answer: Subcontractors are 8%-9% of revenue and management aims to keep them in a broad band; reducing them by 1% would add 15-20 bps margin, but they will not go to zero.

qa_highlights.question: Is customer in-sourcing rising because of AI?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees no AI-driven pattern of in-sourcing; clients instead ask Infosys to take on internal work and use AI to deliver it more efficiently.

risks_watch: Pricing: management expects pricing at the low end of guidance to deteriorate slightly and at the upper end to improve; competitive intensity on AI-productivity-linked deals may persist.
H2 seasonality: furloughs, lower working days and wage hikes in October and January could compress H2 margin toward the lower end.
Q4 manufacturing client impact (close to 1% of growth) and its potential carry-over into FY28.
Mega deal ramp timing and the conversion of large deal TCV ($8.8 bn H1) into revenue.
Retail and Hi-Tech demand weakness and whether it spreads beyond the identified clients; mortgage slowdown in FS.
Macro: 10-year yield near 5%, tariffs and Middle East conflict constraining discretionary spend; US PERM and H-1B changes with unclear cost impact.
summary.management_tone: Confident on AI growth, large deals and margin resilience, but cautious on near-term revenue, with management openly calling Q2 growth below expectations. Evasive on AI margins, year-on-year AI growth and vertical-level guidance, citing non-disclosure.
key_quotes: So the revenue of 10.5% AI, we are sharing is new revenue.
we have been extremely clear that we will only take on the contracts where it meets our economic guidelines.

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth guidance cut to 1%-2% cc from 1.5%-3% (midpoint 1.5%) on pricing pressure and softer volumes; Q2 revenue grew 1.5% YoY cc, and the $5.2 bn TCV with 62% net new and a $2 bn+ mega deal (contributing over 1% to FY28) provide partial backing, while no new capacity is being added and utilization is 85.4%.
